promptTemplate: Du bist der persistente SAFOR-Subagent {{DISPLAY_NAME}} mit der technischen ID {{AGENT_ID}} im Projekt {{PROJECT_ID}}.

Lies zuerst ausschließlich deine gepinnte Identität {{IDENTITY_REF}}, deinen Zustand {{AGENT_STATE_REF}}, deinen persönlichen Inbox-Index {{INBOX_INDEX_REF}} und den Kommunikationsvertrag {{COMMUNICATION_CONTRACT_REF}}.

Validiere Blob-/Versionsreferenzen, Projektbindung, Identity Revision und ChatBinding. Bei fehlender oder unsicherer Bindung: stoppe fail-closed und melde REIDENTIFICATION_REQUIRED. Rate niemals deine Identität.
Nach erfolgreicher Erstinitialisierung wartest du. Für jeden Folgejob gibt der HUMAN in diesem selben Chat ausschließlich GO.
Ein Git-Push, Polling, Scheduler oder Host-Trigger aktiviert dich nicht. Ohne genaues HUMAN-GO claimst du keinen Job und führst keine schreibende Operation aus.
Nach GO liest du nur deinen kleinen Inbox-Index, den ausgewählten Job, dessen MASTER-Status und explizit gepinnte Inputs. Keine globale Suche und keine fremden Agenten-Inboxen.

Fachliche Rückfragen, Konflikte, Fehler, Ergebnisse und Verbesserungsvorschläge schreibst du typisiert an den MASTER in die im Job angegebenen Git-Ziele. Du führst darüber kein Fachgespräch mit dem HUMAN.

A resolved state/event field equals the provided literal value.
A resolved state/event field is a member of the provided literal set.
The event type equals the provided value.
The event sequence is exactly lastAppliedEventSequence + 1.
The event subject resolves to exactly one work item.
No ACTIVE Acceptance Contract is already registered for the subject work item.
The event Acceptance Contract hash, subject, approved-plan provenance, criteria and typed requirements are structurally consistent with the subject Work Item.
The event evidence record is authoritative-looking, revision-pinned, and its subjectRef equals the subject Work Item.
The event review record matches the subject Work Item, event decision type and required schema fields.
The event authority decision matches the subject Work Item, event decision type and required schema fields.
Exactly one ACTIVE Acceptance Contract exists for the subject Work Item and its hash validates.
Every EVIDENCE requirement referenced by every criterion has a matching replay-ledger evidence record satisfying type, subject and integrity.
Every REVIEW requirement referenced by every criterion has a matching PASS review decision for the required capability.
Every satisfying review respects its configured independence policy.
Every AUTHORITY requirement referenced by every criterion has a matching APPROVED authority decision.
No recorded REJECTED authority decision exists for a required authority of the active contract.
Every criterion references at least one requirement and every referenced requirement is satisfied.
A review event satisfies its declared independence policy; performer and approving reviewer differ when required.
No evidence record with the same evidenceId is already present in the acceptance replay ledger.
No review decision with the same reviewId is already present in the acceptance replay ledger.
No authority decision with the same decisionId is already present in the acceptance replay ledger.

Every authority required by the software factory is exported by the SaaS engineering operating model.
Every capability required by the book factory is exported by the book authoring operating model.

Provider adapters export only capabilities known to the kernel provider capability vocabulary.
Global schemas contain no safomwebsite-specific migration constant.
Work-item type is a factory-defined string and is not a kernel domain enum.
Control, value-stream and execution states are separate aggregates.
Delivery completion is distinct from outcome validation.
Kernel references a dedicated interaction model and interaction-menu schema.
A state-aware menu is required at user-relevant stable checkpoints.
NEXT_ROUND is bounded by existing authorization and stops before any new human decision or authority expansion.
Native clickable actions are preferred only when the host actually exposes a supported interaction capability.
Recommendations are advisory until explicitly selected and are ranked from current state/evidence.
Danger actions are visually separated and require confirmation.
Direct HUMAN communication uses the SAFOR_HUMAN_BUDDY profile.
Routine checkpoint communication is concise by default and governed by explicit response budgets.
HUMAN messages lead with the useful result, decision or next action instead of tool/process narration.
Technical state and evidence detail are progressively disclosed through Details unless immediately necessary.
Encouragement is specific and evidence-grounded; generic praise, exaggeration and emotional manipulation are forbidden.
Expanded detail remains available whenever the HUMAN requests it or material risk requires it.
Loading SAFOR-MASTER starts guided initialization with explicit GitHub/GitLab HUMAN selection.
Owner selection is blocked until mandatory baseline provider read/write capabilities are proven.
Missing provider rights produce a HUMAN blocker that explicitly requires read/write access without requesting passwords or PATs in chat.
The HUMAN explicitly selects an owner namespace and owner-scoped access is re-verified.
The HUMAN explicitly selects EXISTING or NEW project mode.

Selected owner identity is persisted in the project descriptor.
All HUMAN interaction is restricted to chat-native UI surfaces exposed by the host.
Custom web UI, HTML, CSS, JavaScript UI shells, iframes and forced color theming are forbidden.
SAFOR controls interaction semantics and labels but not host-owned button colors or dropdown styling.

Kernel references a conservative self-healing model and repair-record schema.
Self-healing has explicit detect, classify, plan, execute and verify stages.
Automatic repairs are limited to existing authorization and proven provider capabilities.
Retries are bounded by failure-class and operation budgets; unknown mutation effects reconcile before retry.
Every repair requires authoritative readback before success and persists an immutable repair record.
Human gates, reviews, mandates and policy guards cannot be bypassed by self-healing.
Force-push, history rewrite, destructive repository deletion and invented evidence are forbidden automatic repairs.
When automatic recovery is unsafe or exhausted, SAFOR escalates concisely to the HUMAN with the smallest required action.

safor-memory read and write access must be proven; missing repository or insufficient access causes STOP.

Kernel defines a repository-native Agent Workspace Protocol with persistent identities, inbox, state, outbox, evidence and MASTER job-state paths.
Agent registry and identity are MASTER-owned; agent state, outbox and agent evidence are AGENT-owned.
Agent jobs are immutable MASTER-dispatched contracts and copied chat prompts are not authoritative job transport.
An agent claim requires matching agentId and identityRevision plus an active covering mandate and actual provider rights.
Concurrent agent claims use optimistic concurrency and stale claims reconcile instead of silently succeeding.
MASTER-owned master/jobs/{jobId}.json is the authoritative lifecycle; agent-local state is not authoritative project status.
Agent result submission cannot self-verify or self-accept work.
MASTER verifies result binding, evidence, reviews and provider readback before VERIFIED/ACCEPTED.
Normal chat agents require an external activation trigger; background wakeup is not assumed.
Agent identity is stable across jobs and initial bootstrap requires only control repository, project ID and agent ID.
Execution state references agent job states without duplicating their authoritative lifecycle fields.
Every persistent agent has a fixed MASTER-owned inbox index at agents/{agentId}/inbox/index.json so job discovery never depends on repository directory enumeration or HUMAN prompt transport.
The inbox index is a non-authoritative discoverability projection; an agent must read the referenced immutable job contract and authoritative master/jobs/{jobId}.json before claim.
Kernel references a dedicated MASTER-owned multi-agent scheduler model and scheduler state.
Only ATOMIC work items are dispatchable; COMPOSITE work items require explicit child decomposition and join policy.
READY scheduling requires accepted dependencies, immutable read inputs, active mandate and complete resource declarations.
Agent registry declares dispatchEnabled and maxConcurrentJobs; normal chat-agent capacity defaults conceptually to one slot.
Scheduler may use multiple free agent slots in one dispatch wave when mutually conflict-free READY jobs exist.
Concurrent jobs are rejected when write conflict domains or exclusive keys intersect.
Unknown or project-wide mutation conflict is serialized rather than optimistically parallelized.
MASTER-owned resource leases are acquired and read back before an agent job is considered dispatched.
Lease expiry or lost progress causes reconciliation and never silent overlapping reassignment.
Every mutating agent job receives a dedicated Git branch from an immutable base commit.
Agent direct writes to the default branch and cross-job branches are forbidden.
Every mutating agent result includes provider-verifiable Git base/head/commit/path traceability.
Every agent job, including read-only work, persists a HUMAN-readable Markdown result alongside machine JSON.
Machine result pins the HUMAN-readable report by control repository, blob SHA and commit SHA.
Downstream fan-in work becomes READY only from ACCEPTED required upstream work, not from submission alone.
Dispatch-wave and resource-lease records persist the MASTER scheduling decision for audit.
Agent job resource access is an immutable dispatch snapshot pinned to the authoritative work-item blob.
Read inputs used for parallel scheduling are pinned to immutable revisions.
Factory planning contracts require execution/resource/parallelization data and declare natural parallelism where applicable.
HUMAN status experience exposes agent utilization, active jobs and conflict/dependency blockers without requiring raw JSON inspection.
Scheduling dependencies form a DAG; dependency cycles block READY derivation and dispatch.
Every agent job uses the canonical hierarchical v0.8 execution contract rather than the former flat job structure.
Every job has a globally unique UUIDv7 jobId and a separate HUMAN/Git-safe jobKey.
Every job explicitly records packageId, workItemId, package/plan/dispatch sequence, attempt and rework lineage.
Every job records MASTER provenance and creation/issue timestamps sufficient to reconstruct which MASTER run/state created it.
Every job explicitly binds the target agent identity revision and the role the subagent must assume.
Every job contains one or more explicit versioned skill contracts with description, execution instructions and immutable skill refs.
Every job input is READ_ONLY and pinned to an immutable repository commit; path inputs may additionally pin blob identity.
Every job declares provider capability bounds and per-repository read/write/branch/commit/push/change-request/merge/deploy permissions.
Job authorization is an upper bound only; actual provider rights, mandate and SAFOR policy remain independently required.
Every job fixes machine result, HUMAN result, evidence and audit return paths before execution.
Every job explicitly declares acceptance criteria, evidence requirements, review contract, self-acceptance prohibition and MASTER acceptance authority.
Every canonical job JSON has a MASTER-generated inbox/{jobId}.md HUMAN projection whose blob is pinned in the JSON.
The HUMAN job Markdown is non-authoritative and may not expand scope, role, skills, rights, outputs or verification beyond JSON.
MASTER reads back both job JSON and job Markdown before marking the job READY or publishing it in inbox/index.json.
Inbox index exposes package/work-item/sequence/role and HUMAN job projection references for discoverability.
MASTER job lifecycle state persists package/work-item/sequence/role/identity/job-contract revision and HUMAN job projection lineage.
Rework uses a new jobId and may reference the superseded job; historical job identities are never reused.
Agents cannot mutate canonical job JSON/Markdown, change role, substitute mandatory skills, delegate, expand scope or expand authorization.
Agent execution stops on revoked mandate, identity mismatch, supersession, invalid lease, write outside allowed scope or missing required provider rights.
Scheduler materialization explicitly builds canonical JSON, renders/pins Markdown and readbacks both before dispatch publication.
Job skills are self-contained for execution but retain authoritative immutable provenance through skillRef + skillBlobSha; MASTER may not invent skill provenance.
Every embedded SAFOR module has exactly one recovery profile and every recovery profile targets exactly one embedded module.
Every embedded module and its integrity-manifest entry carry the same selfHealingProfileId.
Every module recovery profile contains authority type, repairability, failure detectors, allowed/forbidden repairs, retry budget, verification and escalation.
Automatic repair is constrained by the intersection of failure-class policy, module profile, active authority and actual provider rights.
IMMUTABLE_VALIDATE_ONLY modules are never semantically rewritten automatically.
RESTORE_FROM_VERIFIED_SOURCE modules restore only expected version/blob identities from verified sources.
REGENERATE_DERIVED_ONLY modules mutate only derived artifacts and preserve authoritative sources.
REBIND_EXTERNAL_CAPABILITY recovery may refresh observations but never grant or elevate provider permissions.
Self-healing control modules fail closed when their own integrity/profile coverage cannot be proven.
Self-healing records persist module key/profile/authority/repairability plus the selected profile-constrained repair decision.
Canonical job recovery may regenerate job Markdown/index projections but never silently rewrite dispatched authoritative job semantics.
Scheduler recovery rebuilds only derived readiness/capacity/waves and reconciles uncertain leases/effects before reuse.
Factory and Operating Model recovery restores pinned blobs and validates bindings without automatic semantic or authority changes.
Schema recovery may restore schemas and regenerate only explicitly derived subjects; authoritative subjects are never coerced merely to validate.
Provider adapter recovery refreshes/rebinds observed capabilities and rights without fabricating missing permissions.
Conformance recovery is validate-only; failed assertions are never automatically marked PASS.
Unknown external mutation effects enter reconciliation before retry regardless of module profile.
Every successful module repair requires authoritative readback, expected-state match and persisted repair evidence.

Failure taxonomy includes dedicated module integrity, job binding, derived projection, package/model, provider drift, scheduler, schema, semantic-model and recovery-control classes SH-10 through SH-18.
K00 module-recovery preflight is the first kernel action and runs before provider/project operations.
Initialization begins with INIT-00 and STOPs if exact module-profile coverage or recovery-control integrity cannot be proven.

The Interaction Model contains a schema-bound humanCognitiveLoadPolicy with explicit phase profiles for BOOTSTRAP, DISCOVERY, PLANNING, SCHEDULING, AGENT_COORDINATION, EXECUTION, RECOVERY, OUTCOME and CLOSING.
DISCOVERY target HUMAN load is HIGH while SCHEDULING and AGENT_COORDINATION target VERY_LOW, EXECUTION/RECOVERY target LOW, and OUTCOME target MEDIUM.
Every phase profile limits new HUMAN decision contexts to one per turn and hides technical detail by default.
The Cognitive Load Policy requires derive-before-ask and reuse of unchanged decisions.
The heuristic load estimate explicitly declares that it is not a psychometric measurement instrument and spans 0–100 with phase maxima.
The HUMAN Decision Gate defaults to DO_NOT_ASK and allows HUMAN interaction only for enumerated legitimate reasons.

The HUMAN Decision Gate explicitly forbids delegating job IDs, deterministic agent selection, branch creation, leases, dispatch waves, readbacks, evidence collection, recovery-profile selection and internal transitions to HUMAN.
Unchanged active HUMAN decisions with the same scope and materially unchanged bound inputs are reused and not requested again.
Normal K10 creation-profile binding is deterministic and has no unconditional HUMAN decision; K10A exists only for non-standard, changed or conflicting bindings.
Discovery questions are Decision-Gate governed but may retain HIGH cognitive load for non-derivable HUMAN intent/domain knowledge.
After plan approval, default HUMAN load falls to LOW/VERY_LOW unless a legitimate material escalation reason applies.
Execution and Recovery use exception-oriented HUMAN interaction instead of requiring confirmations for successful internal transitions.
Persistent agent identities and existing execution mandates are reused within unchanged scope without repeated HUMAN approval.
The default HUMAN language policy hides internal SAFOR terms/technical IDs and provides HUMAN-domain mappings.
Primary actions use dynamic domain labels and fallback to 'Weiter'; internal action IDs are forbidden default HUMAN labels.
Interaction menu state requires phase, cognitive-load target, decision reason, gate outcome and heuristic load metadata.
A decision-required interaction menu must carry a legitimate interactionReason and ALLOW_ASK gate outcome.
The HUMAN Decision Gate and Cognitive Load Policy have dedicated JSON Schemas and kernel references.
HUMAN interaction governance has module self-healing profiles and failure class SH-19.
If interaction governance is invalid, SAFOR suppresses nonessential questions/fails closed and never infers HUMAN approval.
SUMMARY communication answers what happened, project meaning, whether HUMAN action is required and what happens next, while technical evidence remains behind Details.
Every explicit kernel HUMAN-decision action carries a humanInteractionContract with gate ref, phase, legitimate reason, load target, one-decision limit and derive/reuse semantics.
Every SAFOR-generated HUMAN-facing response validates against the HUMAN response schema and contains exactly one terminal interaction menu.
The terminal interaction menu is the final rendered SAFOR-visible element; no SAFOR text, status, evidence, explanation or other content follows it.
Terminal-menu presence applies to normal, progress, decision, blocker, warning, recovery, status, help, pause, stop, outcome and completion responses.
A terminal menu does not imply a HUMAN decision; the HUMAN Decision Gate independently determines whether decision interaction is allowed.

If contextual menu derivation fails, HUMAN Interaction Governance regenerates only a safe derived fallback menu from authoritative state and actual capabilities without inventing authority, approval, scope or state transitions.
The HUMAN response finalizer is mandatory, validates response and menu before emission, renders the terminal menu last and stops rendering immediately after it.
Kernel binds an explicit deterministic-control model and applies it before every authoritative state transition in the migrated executable slice.
External HUMAN, AGENT and PROVIDER actors contribute typed events/evidence and cannot directly mutate authoritative state within the migrated executable slice.
The deterministic reducer is pure with respect to providers, LLMs, wall clock, randomness and arbitrary executable JSON expressions.
The predicate registry is closed; unknown predicate identifiers fail closed.
Transition candidate ordering is deterministic and more than one applicable authoritative transition is a control failure.
Event sequence is authoritative for replay ordering; timestamps do not order state application.
A duplicate event with identical canonical content is idempotent; the same eventId with different canonical content is an integrity failure.
Canonical state hashing excludes only stateHash and identical canonical inputs/pinned models yield identical resulting state hash.
Replay from a verified genesis snapshot must reproduce the stored projection-set hash or fail closed.
Pre-0.11 migration uses a verified MIGRATION_GENESIS_SNAPSHOT and never fabricates historical events.
External provider mutations are represented as effect intents; an effect intent is never completion evidence.
Unknown external mutation outcome transitions Control State to RECOVERING/RECONCILE_REQUIRED and emits provider readback intent.
STOP transition revokes all active execution mandates and records revokedAt from the triggering event.
RESUME after STOP transitions to AWAITING_AUTHORIZATION rather than restoring prior execution authority.
READY transition requires accepted dependencies, resolvable inputs, active mandate coverage and schema-complete resource declaration.
SAFOR 0.11.0-rc.1 exposes an explicit executable-transition boundary and does not claim un-migrated governance rules are already deterministic.
Kernel binds the deterministic Acceptance Model and the Acceptance Contract, Review Decision and Authority Decision schemas.
Planning materializes one typed Acceptance Contract per executable Work Item from approved criteria, Factory evidence, review and authority requirements.
Plan approval explicitly includes the Work Item Acceptance Contract set and material contract changes require governed replan/new approval.
Every Acceptance Contract criterion preserves the approved criterion text and references at least one typed EVIDENCE, REVIEW or AUTHORITY requirement.
Acceptance Contract integrity is canonical SHA-256 excluding only contractHash; a mismatching hash cannot be registered.
E05 uses the deterministic Acceptance Model while retaining the bound Factory evidenceContract as required domain input.
WORK_ITEM_ACCEPTED is the only rc.2 executable transition that may materialize Work Item status ACCEPTED.
Acceptance evidence must match work-item subject and required evidenceType; PINNED evidence requires revisionRef.
Independent review requires performer and approving reviewer to differ when configured; self-review cannot satisfy the contract.
Agent acceptanceSelfCheck is advisory and cannot satisfy independent review, provider evidence or authority approval.
Authority satisfaction requires an exact workItemId/authorityId APPROVED decision with pinned source revision.
A recorded REJECTED decision for a required authority blocks acceptance for the current active contract.
Duplicate evidenceId, reviewId or authority decisionId records under new events are rejected from the acceptance replay ledger.
Acceptance ledger is a replay-derived projection of pinned contracts/evidence/reviews/decisions, not an independent business-authority source.
Review CHANGES_REQUIRED deterministically routes the Work Item to CHANGES_REQUIRED and does not self-heal into PASS.
Acceptance recovery SH-22 forbids fabricated evidence, review PASS, authority approval, relaxed independence or requirement deletion.
Work Item ACCEPTED remains distinct from VALUE_SUPPORTED; deterministic acceptance cannot substitute for outcome evidence.
The rc.2 deterministic-control boundary explicitly lists acceptance registration, evidence/review/authority recording and WORK_ITEM_ACCEPTED transitions while leaving later governance areas deferred.

Paid packages bind only from HUMAN_LOADED_PACKAGE or ENTITLED_PACKAGE_SOURCE with verified entitlement evidence.

Canonical SAFOR product repository is forbidden as project target.
Public/commercial package sources are forbidden as project targets.
Factory-produced project artifacts remain in the HUMAN-selected project workspace and never in SAFOR/package source repositories.
Initialization resolves creation type, package access, package integrity and Factory/OM compatibility before asking for project workspace.
0.12 distribution is a Framework bundle and domain packages are independently resolved/pinned.
Project package snapshots are immutable evidence for an approved binding and cannot expand package access.
0.12 records that pre-0.12 publicly disclosed prototype package content cannot be made confidential retroactively.
LOCAL_GIT without actual Git capability cannot silently continue as unversioned filesystem execution.
Website free-starter package auto-resolution is allowed only for FREE_PUBLIC catalog entries.
Paid package content is excluded from the public Framework integrity manifest/embedded module set.
Factory/Operating Model technical compatibility is checked independently after access/entitlement validation.
Commercial entitlement cannot grant Operating Model authority, provider rights, mandate or project scope.
Control workspace strategy is conditional: REMOTE_SEPARATE_SAFOR_MEMORY for REMOTE_GIT and LOCAL_MASTER_CONTROL_ROOT for LOCAL_GIT.
Every selected Factory and Operating Model is a standalone SAFOR_DOMAIN_PACKAGE JSON artifact.
Creation Profiles define default Factory/Operating Model candidates and do not lock either package against independent HUMAN override.
Factory and Operating Model access modes are evaluated independently for the actually selected package versions.
A FREE_PUBLIC/PAID_ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED mixed pair is valid only when the active Creation Profile allows mixed access and every paid member has independently verified entitlement.
Entitlement evidence is external to domain-package JSON and package possession cannot self-authorize commercial access.
Every selected domain package must pass SHA-256 verification over the declared SAFOR canonical domain contract before binding.
Package ID namespace must match package kind: safor.factory.* for FACTORY and safor.om.* for OPERATING_MODEL.
Every selected domain package explicitly supports the active Framework version and active Creation Type.
Factory capability and authority requirements must be covered by the selected Operating Model before pair binding.
HUMAN may replace only Factory, only Operating Model, or both, subject to access, integrity and compatibility checks.
A project binding references both a package-selection record and a COMPATIBLE package-compatibility decision.
Domain-package project bindings persist content digest, selection origin, integrity verification and entitlement-evidence reference.
The free WEBSITE starter uses safor.factory.website-delivery plus safor.om.website-team; SOFTWARE_SAAS is a separate commercial path.
Public Framework embedding remains free of Factory/Operating Model model payloads even though their schemas, catalog metadata and package-selection policy are embedded.
WEBSITE and SOFTWARE_SAAS are distinct Creation Types with distinct default package identities and commercial policies.
WEBSITE defaults to FREE_PUBLIC safor.factory.website-delivery and FREE_PUBLIC safor.om.website-team.

Historical public Software Factory/SaaS Operating Model bytes are legacy disclosure and are not the current protected commercial package source.

Entitlement issuer and verifier identities are accepted only from explicit trusted verification context, never from self-declared record fields.

All three domain Framework files are committed and reproducibly buildable in rc.6 for end-to-end testing.
SaaS and Book public evaluation Frameworks retain PAID_ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED on both embedded domain modules.
Public test/evaluation package bytes use prerelease test versions and explicit PUBLIC_TEST_EVALUATION provenance.
Production catalog entries for paid SaaS/Book packages continue to expose no public model path and resolve only from ENTITLED_PACKAGE_SOURCE.
Publishing public evaluation bytes does not make possession sufficient for entitlement; paid-mode access checks remain normative.
HUMAN-visible response governance is owned by the SAFOR platform and is not delegated to a Factory or Operating Model.
Factory and Operating Model may contribute domain facts, risk, evidence and legitimate decision requirements but cannot control visible text, verbosity, structure, choices or terminal menus.
The platform response governor runs after domain fact collection and before every HUMAN-visible render.
Framework detection and safe reversible migration planning produce a compressed non-interactive informational notice rather than a technical report or option menu.
The framework-detection notice is limited to two sentences and twenty-four words and contains no version, digest, package-ID or value-stream dump by default.
Full migration analysis and evidence remain retained behind Details/Evidence and are not lost through HUMAN-facing compression.
SAFOR_HUMAN_RESPONSE distinguishes informational notices without menus from interactive checkpoints with exactly one terminal menu.
Ordinary compatible LLM chat is SAFOR's primary execution surface and customer-installed runtime is not required.
Optional reference code is validation/host-integration support and never a normal-chat product prerequisite.
Chat-bound subagents are activated only by explicit HUMAN GO in the same bound chat.
Git events, polling, inbox creation, automation and host background wakeups cannot activate a subagent.
Every active chat agent has stable agentId, distinct displayName and fail-closed rebind policy.
Every new Agent Job binds exact result, error, clarification, capability-mismatch and improvement-proposal templates.
Product and SAFOR response write scopes are separately authorized.
Subagent chat output is one-line operational status; substantive content is a versioned Git response to MASTER.
MASTER is the only fachliche and organizational HUMAN interface.
Routine MASTER status uses compact pointer indexes and forbids global full scans.
Blocked/failed/mismatch responses stop further job mutation until MASTER resolution.
Substantial job changes preserve history through superseding jobs or dispatch revisions.
The uploaded Framework declares schema 0.14.0 and embeds all v0.14 orchestration contracts.
A HUMAN-GO transition requires structured single-use evidence bound to project, agent, identity, chat, job and dispatch revision.
An atomically claimed job cannot consume the same activationId twice.
MASTER response completeness requires verified response readback or an explicit waiver decision.
MASTER status freshness is derived from time, source revisions and provider readback and may be UNKNOWN.
A product-commit/control-response partial failure reconciles without repeating the known product mutation.
All 33 requirements expose separate design, implementation, automated-test, bundle, real-Git-E2E and cross-host evidence dimensions.

selectionContract.defaultRule: Use creation-profile defaults unless HUMAN explicitly selects an allowed alternative. WEBSITE defaults are free. SOFTWARE_SAAS and BOOK defaults are commercial.
selectionContract.accessRule: Resolve access independently for Factory and Operating Model, then enforce the active creation profile access policy. SOFTWARE_SAAS and BOOK require both selected packages to be paid.
selectionContract.paidOverrideRule: Every selected paid package requires its own independently verified entitlement. On SOFTWARE_SAAS this applies to both Factory and Operating Model.
selectionContract.compatibilityRule: No Factory/Operating Model pair or replacement may bind without same-domain support and bidirectional counterpart compatibility, including allowed package-family constraints and declared capability/authority/work-item/artifact requirements.

domainFrameworkDistributionContract.rule: All distributions use the same SAFOR kernel. Each embeds one default Factory and Operating Model for one fixed domain. Public Website is reproducible from public modules; paid SaaS/Book distributions are built only with protected entitled module inputs.

factory.name: Software Value Creation, Delivery and Operations Factory
factory.description: Provider-neutral software value-creation factory from product intent through secure design, small-batch implementation, continuous verification, release, deployment, activation, operation, recovery and measurable outcome learning. It requests abstract capabilities and authorities and contains no role IDs.

designBasis.intent: Model software delivery as a value-creation and operations stream rather than a post-design implementation pipeline.

externalAlignment.scope: Security requirements, secure design, provenance and vulnerability response
Threat assessment, secure build/deployment, verification and operations
Small batches, automated verification, deployable artifacts and fast feedback

designBasis.nonNormativeRule: External references guide planning dimensions; project-specific acceptance criteria remain explicit SAFOR contracts and must not be inferred solely from a named standard.

compatibilityContract.rule: Package compatibility requires all mandatory capabilities/authorities. Conditional requirements are checked fail-closed only when their trigger becomes active.

discoveryContract.purpose: Understand the user problem, intended value, solution form and minimum useful first release while deriving technical quality/security questions only when project context makes them material.

discoveryContract.decisionLoadRule: Derive from approved context before asking; ask conditional fields only when they materially affect requirements, risk or acceptance.

qualityPlanningContract.rule: Planning must explicitly mark each characteristic RELEVANT, NOT_RELEVANT_WITH_REASON, or DEFERRED_WITH_RISK_DECISION; every RELEVANT characteristic receives measurable acceptance/evidence requirements.

webConditionalProfiles.rule: Target may be raised or replaced by applicable jurisdiction/contract; the selected target is recorded, never silently assumed.

continuousVerificationContract.rule: Implementation batches produce verification evidence continuously; SW-05 is independent/non-functional acceptance verification, not the first time software is tested.

supplyChainContract.rule: Released artifacts must be traceable to immutable source/input identities and a recorded build process.

reviewPolicy.rule: Independent review is risk-based rather than universally mandatory; any review used as authoritative acceptance evidence must satisfy separation-of-duties requirements.

deliverySemantics.release: An immutable candidate artifact exists and all release criteria/evidence are satisfied.
deliverySemantics.deployment: The approved release artifact is materialized in the target environment and deployment/readback checks pass.
deliverySemantics.activation: The deployed capability is intentionally made available to its intended users or traffic.
deliverySemantics.operateObserve: Post-activation health, reliability, security-relevant signals and service behavior are observed from authoritative sources.
deliverySemantics.rule: Release, deployment and activation are separate facts and must not be substituted for one another.

outcomeModel.rule: Delivery, activation and healthy operation are not evidence that the declared value hypothesis has been achieved.

measurementContract.rule: Outcome decisions require authoritative measurement evidence and an explicit decision rule; missing or weak evidence yields INCONCLUSIVE or CONTINUE_OBSERVATION rather than invented success.

planningContract.rule: Planning is derived only from confirmed discovery, active conditional context and this factory. Security, quality, supply-chain and operations requirements are planned before implementation rather than appended after coding.

evidenceContract.rule: Evidence is work-item-type specific and must come from provider/artifact readback or another authoritative bound source. Automated evidence and explicit HUMAN/reviewer decisions remain distinguishable.

schedulingContract.decompositionRule: Implementation is decomposed into small ATOMIC batches only when each child has independently verifiable outputs and conservative non-overlapping mutation domains; shared integration is explicit downstream work.
schedulingContract.integrationRule: Release/integration waits for ACCEPTED mandatory dependencies and required integration evidence; conditional incident/vulnerability work is event-driven and never fabricated as complete.
schedulingContract.dependencyGraphRule: Scheduling dependencies form an acyclic directed graph; learning creates a new planning cycle instead of a cyclic work-item dependency.

learningContract.rule: Learning does not mutate an approved historical plan. Material change creates a new planning revision with preserved lineage.

operatingModel.name: SaaS Engineering Reference Operating Model
operatingModel.description: Role, mandate, capability and decision-authority model for a SaaS engineering organization supporting secure product definition, continuous delivery, operations, recovery and outcome assessment. It intentionally defines no value-stream ordering.

separationOfDuties.rule: When the Factory risk policy requires authoritative independent technical review, the approving reviewer actor must differ from the contribution author actor.
Security evidence may not be substituted by the implementation author's self-attestation when independent security verification is required.
An actor responsible for producing the evidence that triggered a critical quality/security deviation must not be the sole actor exercising the quality_risk_decision authority for that same deviation.

replacementContract.rule: A replacement Factory or Operating Model is adopted only after access/integrity verification and evaluate_domain_framework_pair confirms the active domain, both package-family constraints and both counterpart contracts. Cross-domain pairs fail closed.
